_note: Does a release have to ship with playable recordings?
The 691 mp3s are gitignored (~1 GB), so a build from a fresh clone — which
is what Vercel does — has none of them. They reach production only from an
external host named by VITE_AUDIO_BASE. When that was neither set up nor
noticed, every deploy silently shipped without music and the app told
readers the hymns had never been recorded.

Now true: the 691 recordings live in a Cloudflare R2 bucket and
VITE_AUDIO_BASE points at it. check-audio.mjs samples that URL on every
build, so a release can no longer ship with the music silently missing.
R2 rather than Vercel Blob because the library is 1.0 GB and Blob's free
tier is 1 GB — it did not fit in its own allowance, and going over stops
the store serving for thirty days. R2 allows 10 GB and charges nothing for
egress, which is the right shape for a file people stream repeatedly.
The bucket needs a CORS rule allowing this site to read it. Playback would
work without one, but the fetch that saves a recording for offline use is
blocked cross-origin, so the app would quietly stop working without signal.
